- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off behavior or market panic.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 10-20% of the spike magnitude.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment <0.3), model underperforms; increase forecast by 5-15% to account for suppressed volatility or delayed reaction.
- Model tends to lag in early horizon (1-3 days) when sentiment is volatile; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to reduce lag error.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price; apply a downward bias of 1-3% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model fails to adjust; force a 5-10% downward correction to reflect sentiment shift.
